To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
children with intellectual disabilities show different psychopathological manifestations according to the cognitive and adaptive behavior profiles they are part of.
the cognitive and adaptive behavior profiles of children with intellectual disability are related to their social competence but not to their problematic behaviors.
the cognitive and adaptive profiles of children with intellectual disability are associated to psychopathological manifestations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of profiles of children with intellectual disability based on their cognitive abilities and adaptive behaviors, which are associated with psychopathology.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

children with intellectual disabilities are not more prone to psychopathological disorders than typically developing children, and that the risk of psychopathy is not related to the cognitive functioning or the adaptive behaviors.

children with intellectual disabilities who are non-performing in terms of adaptive behavior and cognitive functions are at higher risk of social maladjustment than those performing and uncooperative.

children who have difficulties with cognitive functioning and adaptive behavior have more social competences problems, while children with cognitive difficulties and good adaptive behavior are at risk to have social competence difficulties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cognitive and behavioral profiles of the children with intellectual disabilities are associated with social competences.

children with intellectual disabilities are not all the same, that their profiles are differentiated by the cognitive functions and the practical abilities of adaptive behavior and that their psychopathological manifestations depend on the viewpoint of the evaluator.
the three clusters differ on their adaptive behavior and cognitive abilities, but not necessarily on psychopathology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to take into account cognitive functioning and adaptive behavior when assessing the psychopathological profile of children with intellectual disability.
the profile of children in terms of cognitive and adaptive behaviors may influence the manifestation of psychopathological symptoms.

it is important for professionals to take into account the cognitive and adaptive functioning profiles of children with intellectual disability in order to better understand their difficulties and to adapt their interventions.
